descriptionChirho: Describing physical spatial extent — land, walls, rivers, places — as wide, broad, or spacious in dimension.
Idiomatic use with a body part (heart, eyes) where 'broad/wide' conveys pride, arrogance, or haughtiness.
Used substantivally with a preposition to denote a broad, open place signifying freedom from constraint or distress.
Idiomatic use with nephesh (soul/appetite) where 'wide/broad' conveys insatiable greed or covetousness.
